Shri Ravi Rahul - Advocate for the appellant.
Shri Mohit Shivhare- Ga appearing for respondents/State.
1.  Heard on I.A. No.6482/2026, which is the third application filed under Section 389 (1) for suspension of sentence on behalf of appellant -Kamal Singh.
Earlier two applications filed by the appellant were withdrawn.

2. The appellant has been convicted for the offence punishable under Sections 354, 506 and 354 ()
376 (2) (i), 376 (AB) of IPC and 3/4, 5 (i), 5 (m) /6 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 ( herein after referred to as 'POCSO Act, 2012' ) and sentenced to undergo maximum sentence of 10 years' RI with maximum fine of Rs.1000/- with default stipulation vide judgment of conviction and order of sentence dated 06.11.2023 passed by the Third Additional Sessions Judge/Special Judge (POCSO) Act, Distt. Vidisha in S.S.T. No. 17/2022.
3.

sentences.text: The case of prosecution in short is that the appellant committed offense on the prosecutrix who at the relevant time was 5-6 years of age on 07/06/2022.
After completion of investigation and on filing of challan, the appellant stands convicted for the offense as state hereinabove in a regular trial conducted by the Sessions Court.
4. The learned counsel appearing for the appellant submits that appellant has been falsely implicated.
There exists previous animosity between the family of the prosecutrix and appellant.

By referring to the evidence of PW-3, the sister of 2 CRA-14645-2023 the prosecutrix, he submits that she admits in her evidence that her husband, Maharaj Singh, is in custody in a murder case wherein,
Sumer Singh and Kamar Singh are witnesses, the learned counsel submits that they belong to the family of the appellant.
He further submits that in her evidence she admits that Hukum Singh is also in jail and there are failed attempts of compromise made between the parties of said case.
He further submits that the mother of the prosecutrix (PW-2), has given her evidence on the basis of story narrated by PW-3 and therefore, her evidence cannot be said to be independent.

That apart, he submits that the appellant has completed three years and five months of custody period, therefore,
his application for grant of suspension of sentence deserves to be allowed.

sentences.text: On the other hand, the learned counsel appearing for the State opposes the application and submits that the prosecutrix who was aged about five-six years at the time of the incident has remained consistent in her statements and allegations against the appellant during the investigation and also before the trial court.
He submits that the medical evidence on record indicates injuries on lips and eyes of the prosecutrix as is evident from Ex. P-8.

He submits that looking to the nature of offence committed by the appellant and the evidence available on record including the DNA report which has been found to be true, no case for grant of suspension of sentence is made out.

6. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
7.
The prosecutrix at the time of incident was aged about 5-6 years.
Her statement recorded before the court clearly made out the offences against the appellant.
The prosecutrix PW-1 in her evidence has clearly stated that the appellant took her along with him, sat on her and inserted his finger in her private part and also slapped her.
The aforesaid statement of prosecutrix remained unrebutted even in her cross-examination.

The eye witness PW-3 who is the sister 3 CRA-14645-2023 of prosecutrix has clearly deposed that when she went to look for her sister, she saw from the hole in the gate that the appellant had removed slacks of the prosecutrix, there were no clothes on the body of the appellant, he was sitting over the prosecutrix tied her mouth and hands with gamcha, slacks of the proxecutrix and was inserting his finger in the private part of the prosecutrix.
The medical evidence available on record indicates the injuries on lip and redness in the eyes of prosecutrix.

8. Apart from the offences for which sentence has been awarded to the appellant, the appellant was also convicted under Section 376 (2) (i) and Section 376 (AB) of IPC, however, in the light of the provisions contained under Section 42 of the POCSO Act, 2012 and Section 71 of IPC, the learned trial Court has awarded sentence to the appellant under Section 3/4 and 5 (i), 5 (m)/6 of POCSO Act, 2012 9.

In view of the aforesaid facts, having been found to be established in the trial, this court is not inclined to allow the application (I.A. No. 6482/2026) for grant of suspension of sentence and therefore, the same stands rejected.
( AMIT
